wdi-IS.AIR.PSGR.label: Air transport, passengers carried
wdi-IS.AIR.PSGR.provider:
Civil Aviation Statistics of the World, International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), uri: https://data.icao.int/newdataplus/#:~:text=ICAO%20data%20is%20comprised%20of,information%20about%20commercial%20air%20carriers;
ICAO Staff estimates, International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), uri: https://data.icao.int/newdataplus/#:~:text=ICAO%20data%20is%20comprised%20of,information%20about%20commercial%20air%20carriers
wdi-IS.AIR.PSGR.definition: Air carrier data per country refers to passengers carried by airlines registered in that country regardless of the origin or destination of the passengers.
wdi-IS.AIR.PSGR.prompt: How many passenger boardings did airlines registered in {place} carry in {year}?
wdi-IS.AIR.PSGR.scope: Domestic and international flights by airlines registered there. A connection can count twice.
wdi-IS.AIR.PSGR.route: Estimate the fleets of the major local airlines, flights per aircraft per day and seats filled. Add smaller carriers and multiply by operating days.

wdi-IS.AIR.DPRT.label: Air transport, registered carrier departures worldwide
wdi-IS.AIR.DPRT.provider:
Civil Aviation Statistics of the World, International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), uri: https://data.icao.int/newdataplus/#:~:text=ICAO%20data%20is%20comprised%20of,information%20about%20commercial%20air%20carriers;
ICAO Staff estimates, International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), uri: https://data.icao.int/newdataplus/#:~:text=ICAO%20data%20is%20comprised%20of,information%20about%20commercial%20air%20carriers
wdi-IS.AIR.DPRT.definition: Registered carrier departures worldwide are domestic takeoffs and takeoffs abroad of air carriers registered in the country.
wdi-IS.AIR.DPRT.prompt: How many flights did airlines registered in {place} operate in {year}?
wdi-IS.AIR.DPRT.scope: Count takeoffs by registered carriers, including those outside the country.
wdi-IS.AIR.DPRT.route: Estimate the number of active aircraft and their trips per day. Short-haul planes can make several flights in the time a long-haul plane makes one.

wdi-IS.AIR.GOOD.MT.K1.label: Air transport, freight (million ton-km)
wdi-IS.AIR.GOOD.MT.K1.provider:
Civil Aviation Statistics of the World, International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), uri: https://data.icao.int/newdataplus/#:~:text=ICAO%20data%20is%20comprised%20of,information%20about%20commercial%20air%20carriers;
ICAO Staff estimates, International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), uri: https://data.icao.int/newdataplus/#:~:text=ICAO%20data%20is%20comprised%20of,information%20about%20commercial%20air%20carriers
wdi-IS.AIR.GOOD.MT.K1.definition: Air freight is the volume of freight, express, and diplomatic bags carried on each flight stage (operation of an aircraft from takeoff to its next landing), measured in metric tons times kilometers traveled.
wdi-IS.AIR.GOOD.MT.K1.prompt: How much air freight work did airlines registered in {place} do in {year}?
wdi-IS.AIR.GOOD.MT.K1.scope: Weight multiplied by distance. One tonne carried one kilometre is one tonne-kilometre.
wdi-IS.AIR.GOOD.MT.K1.route: Estimate loaded cargo on dedicated freighters and in passenger-plane holds, then multiply by trips and the distance flown.

wdi-IS.RRS.PASG.KM.label: Railways, passengers carried (million passenger-km)
wdi-IS.RRS.PASG.KM.provider:
Railisa Database (UIC), International Union of Railways (UIC), uri: https://uic-stats.uic.org/select/;
OECD Statistics, Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
wdi-IS.RRS.PASG.KM.definition: Passengers carried by railway are the number of passengers transported by rail multiplied by kilometers traveled.
wdi-IS.RRS.PASG.KM.prompt: How far did railway passengers travel in total in {place} in {year}?
wdi-IS.RRS.PASG.KM.scope: One passenger travelling one kilometre counts as one passenger-kilometre. Use the national railway statistics.
wdi-IS.RRS.PASG.KM.route: Separate repeated short commuter journeys from rarer long-distance trips. Estimate how many of each happen and multiply by typical trip length.

wdi-IS.RRS.GOOD.MT.K6.label: Railways, goods transported (million ton-km)
wdi-IS.RRS.GOOD.MT.K6.provider:
Railisa Database (UIC), International Union of Railways (UIC), uri: https://uic-stats.uic.org/select/;
OECD Statistics, Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
wdi-IS.RRS.GOOD.MT.K6.definition: Goods transported by railway are the volume of goods transported by railway, measured in metric tons times kilometers traveled.
wdi-IS.RRS.GOOD.MT.K6.prompt: How much freight work did the railways of {place} do in {year}?
wdi-IS.RRS.GOOD.MT.K6.scope: One tonne of freight moved one kilometre counts as one tonne-kilometre.
wdi-IS.RRS.GOOD.MT.K6.route: Think of the major freight flows, such as grain, minerals or containers. Estimate trains per day, tonnes per train and their average haul.

wdi-IS.RRS.TOTL.KM.label: Rail lines (total route-km)
wdi-IS.RRS.TOTL.KM.provider: Railisa Database, International Union of Railways (UIC), uri: https://uic-stats.uic.org/
wdi-IS.RRS.TOTL.KM.definition: The total length of rail line in the country operated for passenger transport, goods transport, or both.
wdi-IS.RRS.TOTL.KM.prompt: How long was the railway network of {place} in {year}?
wdi-IS.RRS.TOTL.KM.scope: Route length. A line with two parallel tracks counts once.
wdi-IS.RRS.TOTL.KM.route: Sketch a map connecting the main cities, estimate their separations and add branches. Avoid counting both tracks of the same line.

wdi-IS.SHP.GOOD.TU.label: Container port traffic (TEU: 20 foot equivalent units)
wdi-IS.SHP.GOOD.TU.provider: UN Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), uri: http://unctad.org/en/Pages/statistics.aspx
wdi-IS.SHP.GOOD.TU.definition: Port container traffic measures the flow of containers from land to sea transport modes, and vice versa, in twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs), a standard-size container. Data refer to coastal shipping as well as international journeys. Transshipment traffic is counted as two lifts at the intermediate port (once to off-load and again as an outbound lift) and includes empty units.
wdi-IS.SHP.GOOD.TU.prompt: How much container traffic passed through ports in {place} in {year}?
wdi-IS.SHP.GOOD.TU.scope: Twenty-foot equivalent units (TEU). A 40-foot container counts as two TEU. Include transshipment.
wdi-IS.SHP.GOOD.TU.route: Estimate how many large container ships call per week and how many boxes they actually move at each port. Containers carried onward by another ship can add to the count.

wdi-ST.INT.ARVL.label: International tourism, number of arrivals
wdi-ST.INT.ARVL.provider: Yearbook of Tourism Statistics, Compendium of Tourism Statistics and data files, UN Tourism
wdi-ST.INT.ARVL.definition: International inbound tourists (overnight visitors) are the number of tourists who travel to a country other than that in which they have their usual residence, but outside their usual environment, for a period not exceeding 12 months and whose main purpose in visiting is other than an activity remunerated from within the country visited. When data on number of tourists are not available, the number of visitors, which includes tourists, same-day visitors, cruise passengers, and crew members, is shown instead. Sources and collection methods for arrivals differ across countries. In some cases data are from border statistics (police, immigration, and the like) and supplemented by border surveys. In other cases data are from tourism accommodation establishments. For some countries number of arrivals is limited to arrivals by air and for others to arrivals staying in hotels. Some countries include arrivals of nationals residing abroad while others do not. Caution should thus be used in comparing arrivals across countries. The data on inbound tourists refer to the number of arrivals, not to the number of people traveling. Thus a person who makes several trips to a country during a given period is counted each time as a new arrival.
wdi-ST.INT.ARVL.prompt: How many international tourist arrivals did {place} record in {year}?
wdi-ST.INT.ARVL.scope: Use the published arrivals series. Repeat visitors can be counted again. Reporting may use border or accommodation records.
wdi-ST.INT.ARVL.route: Estimate the number of international visitors the main holiday areas and cities can host per day. Multiply across the year and allow for seasonality.

wdi-ST.INT.DPRT.label: International tourism, number of departures
wdi-ST.INT.DPRT.provider: Yearbook of Tourism Statistics, Compendium of Tourism Statistics and data files, UN Tourism
wdi-ST.INT.DPRT.definition: International outbound tourists are the number of departures that people make from their country of usual residence to any other country for any purpose other than a remunerated activity in the country visited. The data on outbound tourists refer to the number of departures, not to the number of people traveling. Thus a person who makes several trips from a country during a given period is counted each time as a new departure.
wdi-ST.INT.DPRT.prompt: How many outbound international tourism departures did {place} record in {year}?
wdi-ST.INT.DPRT.scope: Count trips rather than unique residents.
wdi-ST.INT.DPRT.route: Estimate residents able to travel abroad, how often they do so and how much cross-border travel can happen by road or rail.

wdi-IT.CEL.SETS.label: Mobile cellular subscriptions
wdi-IT.CEL.SETS.provider: World Telecommunication/ICT Indicators Database, International Telecommunication Union (ITU)
wdi-IT.CEL.SETS.definition: Mobile cellular telephone subscriptions are subscriptions to a public mobile telephone service that provide access to the PSTN using cellular technology. The indicator includes (and is split into) the number of postpaid subscriptions, and the number of active prepaid accounts (i.e. that have been used during the last three months). The indicator applies to all mobile cellular subscriptions that offer voice communications. It excludes subscriptions via data cards or USB modems, subscriptions to public mobile data services, private trunked mobile radio, telepoint, radio paging and telemetry services.
wdi-IT.CEL.SETS.prompt: How many mobile phone subscriptions were active in {place} in {year}?
wdi-IT.CEL.SETS.scope: Subscriptions, including active prepaid accounts. A person can have more than one.
wdi-IT.CEL.SETS.route: Estimate adult residents with phones, then add work phones and second SIM cards. Children and shared phones pull the estimate in the other direction.

wdi-IT.NET.BBND.label: Fixed broadband subscriptions
wdi-IT.NET.BBND.provider: World Telecommunication/ICT Indicators Database, International Telecommunication Union (ITU)
wdi-IT.NET.BBND.definition: Fixed broadband subscriptions refers to fixed subscriptions to high-speed access to the public Internet (a TCP/IP connection), at downstream speeds equal to, or greater than, 256 kbit/s. This includes cable modem, DSL, fiber-to-the-home/building, other fixed (wired)-broadband subscriptions, satellite broadband and terrestrial fixed wireless broadband. This total is measured irrespective of the method of payment. It excludes subscriptions that have access to data communications (including the Internet) via mobile-cellular networks. It should include fixed WiMAX and any other fixed wireless technologies. It includes both residential subscriptions and subscriptions for organizations.
wdi-IT.NET.BBND.prompt: How many fixed broadband subscriptions did {place} have in {year}?
wdi-IT.NET.BBND.scope: Fixed connections such as fibre and cable. Exclude mobile data subscriptions.
wdi-IT.NET.BBND.route: Estimate households, decide what fraction have a fixed connection and add businesses. One household can share a connection among several people.

wdi-IT.MLT.MAIN.label: Fixed telephone subscriptions
wdi-IT.MLT.MAIN.provider: World Telecommunication/ICT Indicators Database, International Telecommunication Union (ITU)
wdi-IT.MLT.MAIN.definition: Fixed telephone subscriptions refers to the sum of active number of analogue fixed telephone lines, voice-over-IP (VoIP) subscriptions, fixed wireless local loop (WLL) subscriptions, ISDN voice-channel equivalents and fixed public payphones.
wdi-IT.MLT.MAIN.prompt: How many fixed telephone subscriptions remained in {place} in {year}?
wdi-IT.MLT.MAIN.scope: Use the fixed telephone series. Include fixed voice subscriptions that use internet technology where reported.
wdi-IT.MLT.MAIN.route: Think about households that kept a fixed number after getting mobile phones, plus shops and offices that still need a public contact number.

wdi-EG.USE.ELEC.KH.PC.label: Electric power consumption (kWh per capita)
wdi-EG.USE.ELEC.KH.PC.provider: IEA Energy Statistics Data Browser, International Energy Agency (IEA), uri: https://www.iea.org/data-and-statistics/data-tools/energy-statistics-data-browser, publisher: International Energy Agency (IEA), date accessed: 2025-03-25
wdi-EG.USE.ELEC.KH.PC.definition: Electric power consumption measures the production of power plants and combined heat and power plants less transmission, distribution, and transformation losses and own use by heat and power plants.
wdi-EG.USE.ELEC.KH.PC.prompt: How much electricity was used per resident in {place} in {year}?
wdi-EG.USE.ELEC.KH.PC.scope: Annual per-person allocation of economy-wide electricity use. Include industry and services.
wdi-EG.USE.ELEC.KH.PC.route: Start from what a household uses for lighting, cooling and appliances. Divide by people in the household, then allow for workplaces and industry.

wdi-ER.FSH.AQUA.MT.label: Aquaculture production (metric tons)
wdi-ER.FSH.AQUA.MT.provider: Food and Agriculture Organization., Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
wdi-ER.FSH.AQUA.MT.definition: Aquaculture is understood to mean the farming of aquatic organisms including fish, molluscs, crustaceans and aquatic plants. Aquaculture production specifically refers to output from aquaculture activities, which are designated for final harvest for consumption.
wdi-ER.FSH.AQUA.MT.prompt: How much did aquaculture produce in {place} in {year}?
wdi-ER.FSH.AQUA.MT.scope: Use the FAO aquaculture production series, which can include aquatic plants. Exclude wild capture.
wdi-ER.FSH.AQUA.MT.route: Think of farmed species, numbers of ponds or cages and harvests per year. Compare farm output with domestic seafood demand and exports.

wdi-ER.FSH.CAPT.MT.label: Capture fisheries production (metric tons)
wdi-ER.FSH.CAPT.MT.provider: Food and Agriculture Organization., Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
wdi-ER.FSH.CAPT.MT.definition: Capture fisheries production measures the volume of fish catches landed by a country for all commercial, industrial, recreational and subsistence purposes.
wdi-ER.FSH.CAPT.MT.prompt: How much did capture fisheries produce in {place} in {year}?
wdi-ER.FSH.CAPT.MT.scope: Use the FAO capture production series. Exclude aquaculture.
wdi-ER.FSH.CAPT.MT.route: Estimate the working fishing fleet, fishing days and catch per boat per trip. Allow for the difference between small coastal boats and industrial vessels.

wdi-ER.H2O.FWTL.K3.label: Annual freshwater withdrawals, total (billion cubic meters)
wdi-ER.H2O.FWTL.K3.provider: AQUASTAT - FAO's Global Information System on Water and Agriculture, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), uri: https://data.apps.fao.org/aquastat/, publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), date accessed: 20240529
wdi-ER.H2O.FWTL.K3.definition: Annual freshwater withdrawals refer to total water withdrawals, not counting evaporation losses from storage basins. Withdrawals also include water from desalination plants in countries where they are a significant source. Withdrawals can exceed 100 percent of total renewable resources where extraction from nonrenewable aquifers or desalination plants is considerable or where there is significant water reuse. Withdrawals for agriculture and industry are total withdrawals for irrigation and livestock production and for direct industrial use (including withdrawals for cooling thermoelectric plants). Withdrawals for domestic uses include drinking water, municipal use or supply, and use for public services, commercial establishments, and homes.
wdi-ER.H2O.FWTL.K3.prompt: How much freshwater did {place} withdraw in {year}?
wdi-ER.H2O.FWTL.K3.scope: Annual freshwater withdrawals for agriculture, industry and households. Count water withdrawn, including water returned later.
wdi-ER.H2O.FWTL.K3.route: Household taps are only one part. Estimate irrigated land and the depth of water applied over a year, then add industrial and household withdrawals.

wdi-ER.H2O.INTR.K3.label: Renewable internal freshwater resources, total (billion cubic meters)
wdi-ER.H2O.INTR.K3.provider: AQUASTAT - FAO's Global Information System on Water and Agriculture, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), uri: https://data.apps.fao.org/aquastat/, publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), date accessed: 20240529
wdi-ER.H2O.INTR.K3.definition: Renewable internal freshwater resources flows refer to internal renewable resources (internal river flows and groundwater from rainfall) in the country.
wdi-ER.H2O.INTR.K3.prompt: How much renewable freshwater is generated internally in {place} in a typical year?
wdi-ER.H2O.INTR.K3.scope: Use the long-term average reported in the {year} data. Include runoff and groundwater recharge from precipitation within the country, accounting for overlap.
wdi-ER.H2O.INTR.K3.route: Estimate land area and average rain depth, then the fraction left after evaporation and plant use. Do not count river water flowing in from another country.

wdi-AG.LND.FRST.K2.label: Forest area (sq. km)
wdi-AG.LND.FRST.K2.provider: FAOSTAT, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), uri: https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/RL, publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
wdi-AG.LND.FRST.K2.definition: Forest area is land under natural or planted stands of trees of at least 5 meters in situ, whether productive or not, and excludes tree stands in agricultural production systems (for example, in fruit plantations and agroforestry systems) and trees in urban parks and gardens.
wdi-AG.LND.FRST.K2.prompt: How much of {place} was classified as forest in {year}?
wdi-AG.LND.FRST.K2.scope: Use the FAO forest-area definition. The land use matters, so tree-covered orchards do not automatically count.
wdi-AG.LND.FRST.K2.route: Picture the map in regions. Estimate the size and forest cover of the mountainous, agricultural and urban parts separately.

wdi-AG.LND.CREL.HA.label: Land under cereal production (hectares)
wdi-AG.LND.CREL.HA.provider: FAO electronic files and web site, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), uri: https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/QCL, note: Item code F1717, publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
wdi-AG.LND.CREL.HA.definition: Land under cereal production refers to harvested area, although some countries report only sown or cultivated area. Cereals include wheat, rice, maize, barley, oats, rye, millet, sorghum, buckwheat, and mixed grains. Production data on cereals relate to crops harvested for dry grain only. Cereal crops harvested for hay or harvested green for food, feed, or silage and those used for grazing are excluded.
wdi-AG.LND.CREL.HA.prompt: How much land did {place} harvest for cereal grain in {year}?
wdi-AG.LND.CREL.HA.scope: Harvested area under cereals. Count grain crops, excluding cereals harvested green for forage.
wdi-AG.LND.CREL.HA.route: Estimate cereal consumption and export needs, then divide by grain harvested per hectare. A double-cropped field can contribute multiple harvests.

wdi-AG.CON.FERT.ZS.label: Fertilizer consumption (kilograms per hectare of arable land)
wdi-AG.CON.FERT.ZS.provider: FAO electronic files and web site, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
wdi-AG.CON.FERT.ZS.definition: Fertilizer consumption measures the quantity of plant nutrients used per unit of arable land. Fertilizer products cover nitrogenous, potash, and phosphate fertilizers (including ground rock phosphate). Traditional nutrients--animal and plant manures--are not included. For the purpose of data dissemination, FAO has adopted the concept of a calendar year (January to December). Some countries compile fertilizer data on a calendar year basis, while others are on a split-year basis. Arable land includes land defined by the FAO as land under temporary crops (double-cropped areas are counted once), temporary meadows for mowing or for pasture, land under market or kitchen gardens, and land temporarily fallow. Land abandoned as a result of shifting cultivation is excluded.
wdi-AG.CON.FERT.ZS.prompt: How much fertiliser was used per hectare of arable land in {place} in {year}?
wdi-AG.CON.FERT.ZS.scope: Plant nutrient content in the World Bank measure. Exclude traditional animal and plant manures.
wdi-AG.CON.FERT.ZS.route: Think of a crop’s nutrient needs and how much is already in the soil. Compare high-yield irrigated crops with fields that receive little manufactured fertiliser.

wdi-SH.MED.BEDS.ZS.label: Hospital beds (per 1,000 people)
wdi-SH.MED.BEDS.ZS.provider: WHO data, supplemented by country data, World Health Organization (WHO)
wdi-SH.MED.BEDS.ZS.definition: Hospital beds include inpatient beds available in public, private, general, and specialized hospitals and rehabilitation centers. In most cases beds for both acute and chronic care are included.
wdi-SH.MED.BEDS.ZS.prompt: How many hospital beds were available for every 1,000 residents in {place} in {year}?
wdi-SH.MED.BEDS.ZS.scope: Use the World Bank’s hospital-bed series. Definitions and coverage differ among health systems.
wdi-SH.MED.BEDS.ZS.route: Estimate how often people need an overnight stay and how many nights each admission takes. Convert total bed-days to staffed beds and allow for spare capacity.

wdi-SH.MED.PHYS.ZS.label: Physicians (per 1,000 people)
wdi-SH.MED.PHYS.ZS.definition: Physicians include generalist and specialist medical practitioners.
wdi-SH.MED.PHYS.ZS.prompt: How many physicians were recorded for every 1,000 residents in {place} in {year}?
wdi-SH.MED.PHYS.ZS.scope: The source covers generalist and specialist medical practitioners. It does not count all health workers.
wdi-SH.MED.PHYS.ZS.route: Think about patient panels for primary care and the additional doctors needed in hospitals. Scale that to a town of a thousand residents.

wdi-SE.PRM.ENRL.label: Primary education, pupils
wdi-SE.PRM.ENRL.provider: Data API, UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), uri: https://databrowser.uis.unesco.org/resources, note: The data are obtained through the UIS API.  Detailed documentation is available at: https://api.uis.unesco.org/api/public/documentation/, publisher: UNESCO Institute for Statistics (UIS), type: Bulk file (csv), date accessed: 2026-03-19, date published: 2026-02
wdi-SE.PRM.ENRL.definition: Primary education pupils is the total number of pupils enrolled at primary level in public and private schools.
wdi-SE.PRM.ENRL.prompt: How many pupils were enrolled in primary education in {place} in {year}?
wdi-SE.PRM.ENRL.scope: Count enrolled pupils of any age in primary education.
wdi-SE.PRM.ENRL.route: Estimate a typical birth cohort from the population and birth rate, then multiply by primary grades and adjust for enrolment and repeated grades.

wdi-SE.PRM.TCHR.label: Primary education, teachers
wdi-SE.PRM.TCHR.provider: Data API, UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), uri: https://databrowser.uis.unesco.org/resources, note: The data are obtained through the UIS API.  Detailed documentation is available at: https://api.uis.unesco.org/api/public/documentation/, publisher: UNESCO Institute for Statistics (UIS), type: Bulk file (csv), date accessed: 2026-03-19, date published: 2026-02
wdi-SE.PRM.TCHR.definition: Primary education, teachers refers to the total number of teachers at primary level, including full-time and part-time teachers.
wdi-SE.PRM.TCHR.prompt: How many teachers worked at primary level in {place} in {year}?
wdi-SE.PRM.TCHR.scope: Use the published primary teacher count.
wdi-SE.PRM.TCHR.route: Estimate the number of primary-age pupils, then how many pupils each teacher can teach. Allow for small schools, specialists and teachers who share a class.

wdi-SE.SEC.ENRL.VO.label: Secondary education, vocational pupils
wdi-SE.SEC.ENRL.VO.provider: Stat Bulk Data Download Service, UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), uri: https://uis.unesco.org/bdds, publisher: UNESCO Institute for Statistics (UIS)
wdi-SE.SEC.ENRL.VO.definition: Secondary vocational pupils are the number of secondary students enrolled in technical and vocational education programs, including teacher training.
wdi-SE.SEC.ENRL.VO.prompt: How many secondary pupils were enrolled in vocational programmes in {place} in {year}?
wdi-SE.SEC.ENRL.VO.scope: Secondary-level vocational programmes only, as classified by the source.
wdi-SE.SEC.ENRL.VO.route: Estimate secondary-age cohorts, enrolment and the share choosing technical or vocational tracks. Systems differ in when pupils can specialise.

wdi-SP.DYN.CBRT.IN.label: Birth rate, crude (per 1,000 people)
wdi-SP.DYN.CBRT.IN.definition: Crude birth rate indicates the number of live births occurring during the year, per 1,000 population estimated at midyear. Subtracting the crude death rate from the crude birth rate provides the rate of natural increase, which is equal to the rate of population change in the absence of migration.
wdi-SP.DYN.CBRT.IN.prompt: How many babies were born per 1,000 residents in {place} in {year}?
wdi-SP.DYN.CBRT.IN.scope: Live births divided by midyear population, expressed per 1,000 residents.
wdi-SP.DYN.CBRT.IN.route: Picture a town of a thousand. Estimate the fraction in childbearing ages and how many in that group would have a baby in a year.

wdi-SP.DYN.CDRT.IN.label: Death rate, crude (per 1,000 people)
wdi-SP.DYN.CDRT.IN.definition: Crude death rate indicates the number of deaths occurring during the year, per 1,000 population estimated at midyear. Subtracting the crude death rate from the crude birth rate provides the rate of natural increase, which is equal to the rate of population change in the absence of migration.
wdi-SP.DYN.CDRT.IN.prompt: How many people died per 1,000 residents in {place} in {year}?
wdi-SP.DYN.CDRT.IN.scope: All deaths divided by midyear population, expressed per 1,000 residents.
wdi-SP.DYN.CDRT.IN.route: Start with the lifespan of a hypothetical stable population. Then think about whether this country has more children or older residents than that simple model.

wdi-SP.DYN.TFRT.IN.label: Fertility rate, total (births per woman)
wdi-SP.DYN.TFRT.IN.definition: Total fertility rate represents the number of children that would be born to a woman if she were to live to the end of her childbearing years and bear children in accordance with age-specific fertility rates of the specified year.
wdi-SP.DYN.TFRT.IN.prompt: What family size do the {year} birth rates of {place} imply?
wdi-SP.DYN.TFRT.IN.scope: Total fertility rate. It applies that year’s age-specific rates across a hypothetical woman’s reproductive life.
wdi-SP.DYN.TFRT.IN.route: Compare common family sizes and the share of people who never have children. Think about how birth timing can shift the rate in a given year.

wdi-SE.TER.ENRR.label: School enrollment, tertiary (% gross)
wdi-SE.TER.ENRR.provider: Data API, UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), uri: https://databrowser.uis.unesco.org/resources, note: The data are obtained through the UIS API.  Detailed documentation is available at: https://api.uis.unesco.org/api/public/documentation/, publisher: UNESCO Institute for Statistics (UIS), type: Bulk file (csv), date accessed: 2026-03-19, date published: 2026-02
wdi-SE.TER.ENRR.definition: Gross enrollment ratio is the ratio of total enrollment, regardless of age, to the population of the age group that officially corresponds to the level of education shown. Tertiary education, whether or not to an advanced research qualification, normally requires, as a minimum condition of admission, the successful completion of education at the secondary level.
wdi-SE.TER.ENRR.prompt: What was the gross tertiary enrolment ratio in {place} in {year}?
wdi-SE.TER.ENRR.scope: Enrolled tertiary students of any age divided by the population of the official tertiary-age group. It can exceed 100%.
wdi-SE.TER.ENRR.route: Estimate how many school leavers enter tertiary study and how long they stay. Include returning adult students and international students.

wdi-SH.IMM.IDPT.label: Immunization, DPT (% of children ages 12-23 months)
wdi-SH.IMM.IDPT.provider:
World Health Organization (WHO), uri: http://www.who.int/immunization/monitoring_surveillance/en/;
UN Children's Fund (UNICEF)
wdi-SH.IMM.IDPT.definition: Child immunization, DPT, measures the percentage of children ages 12-23 months who received DPT vaccinations before 12 months or at any time before the survey. A child is considered adequately immunized against diphtheria, pertussis (or whooping cough), and tetanus (DPT) after receiving three doses of vaccine.
wdi-SH.IMM.IDPT.prompt: What share of children aged 12–23 months had received three DPT vaccine doses in {place} in {year}?
wdi-SH.IMM.IDPT.scope: Use the WHO and UNICEF estimate reported by the World Bank. DPT covers diphtheria, pertussis and tetanus.
wdi-SH.IMM.IDPT.route: Think about how often families can reach routine child health services and how much follow-up is needed to complete several doses.

wdi-EG.ELC.ACCS.RU.ZS.label: Access to electricity, rural (% of rural population)
wdi-EG.ELC.ACCS.RU.ZS.provider: SDG 7.1.1 Electrification Dataset, World Bank (WB), uri: https://trackingsdg7.esmap.org/downloads, note: Data is downloaded from ESMAP website. Data is released when a new Tracking SDG7 report is released., publisher: World Bank (WB), date accessed: 2024-05-16, date published: 2023
wdi-EG.ELC.ACCS.RU.ZS.definition: Access to electricity, rural is the percentage of rural population with access to electricity.
wdi-EG.ELC.ACCS.RU.ZS.prompt: What share of rural residents had access to electricity in {place} in {year}?
wdi-EG.ELC.ACCS.RU.ZS.scope: Use the published rural access estimate. Access can include off-grid sources and does not establish that power is reliable.
wdi-EG.ELC.ACCS.RU.ZS.route: Think about where villages sit relative to the grid, how difficult the terrain is and whether local solar or mini-grids cover more remote households.

wdi-SH.H2O.BASW.RU.ZS.label: People using at least basic drinking water services, rural (% of rural population)
wdi-SH.H2O.BASW.RU.ZS.provider:
WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP) for Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene, World Health Organization (WHO), uri: washdata.org, publisher: WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP) for Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene (washdata.org), date accessed: 2025-09-30, date published: 2025-08-25;
UN Children's Fund (UNICEF), uri: washdata.org, note: WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP) for Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene
wdi-SH.H2O.BASW.RU.ZS.definition: The percentage of people using at least basic water services.  This indicator encompasses both people using basic water services as well as those using safely managed water services.  Basic drinking water services is defined as drinking water from an improved source, provided collection time is not more than 30 minutes for a round trip.  Improved water sources include piped water, boreholes or tubewells, protected dug wells, protected springs, and packaged or delivered water.
wdi-SH.H2O.BASW.RU.ZS.prompt: What share of rural residents in {place} used at least basic drinking-water services in {year}?
wdi-SH.H2O.BASW.RU.ZS.scope: An improved source reachable within a round trip of 30 minutes, including queuing.
wdi-SH.H2O.BASW.RU.ZS.route: Consider how many people are reached by pipes, protected wells or community taps. Add the constraint that the water source needs to be close enough.

wdi-SH.STA.SMSS.ZS.label: People using safely managed sanitation services (% of population)
wdi-SH.STA.SMSS.ZS.provider:
WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP) for Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene, World Health Organization (WHO), uri: washdata.org, note: Aggregate data by groups are computed based on the groupings for the World Bank fiscal year in which the data was released by the WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP) for Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene., publisher: WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP) for Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene (washdata.org), date accessed: 2025-09-30, date published: 2025-08-25;
UN Children's Fund (UNICEF), uri: washdata.org, note: WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP) for Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene
wdi-SH.STA.SMSS.ZS.definition: The percentage of people using improved sanitation facilities that are not shared with other households and where excreta are safely disposed of in situ or transported and treated offsite. Improved sanitation facilities include flush/pour flush to piped sewer systems, septic tanks or pit latrines: ventilated improved pit latrines, composting toilets or pit latrines with slabs.
wdi-SH.STA.SMSS.ZS.prompt: What share of residents in {place} used safely managed sanitation in {year}?
wdi-SH.STA.SMSS.ZS.scope: An improved, unshared facility with excreta safely disposed of in place or treated elsewhere.
wdi-SH.STA.SMSS.ZS.route: Think about sewer connections and treatment, plus septic systems that are safely managed. Having a toilet alone does not tell you where waste goes.

wdi-SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS.label: Employment in agriculture (% of total employment) (modeled ILO estimate)
wdi-SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS.provider: ILO Modelled Estimates database (ILOEST), International Labour Organization (ILO), uri: https://ilostat.ilo.org/data/bulk/, publisher: ILOSTAT, type: external database, date accessed: January 17, 2026
wdi-SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS.definition: Employment is defined as persons of working age who were engaged in any activity to produce goods or provide services for pay or profit, whether at work during the reference period or not at work due to temporary absence from a job, or to working-time arrangement. The agriculture sector consists of activities in agriculture, hunting, forestry and fishing, in accordance with division 1 (ISIC 2) or categories A-B (ISIC 3) or category A (ISIC 4).
wdi-SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS.prompt: What share of employed people in {place} worked in agriculture in {year}?
wdi-SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS.scope: ILO modelled estimate for agriculture, hunting, forestry and fishing. Use share of employment.
wdi-SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS.route: Estimate how urban the workforce is and how much farming is mechanised. A large agricultural output need not mean a large farm workforce.

wdi-SL.IND.EMPL.ZS.label: Employment in industry (% of total employment) (modeled ILO estimate)
wdi-SL.IND.EMPL.ZS.provider: ILO Modelled Estimates database (ILOEST), International Labour Organization (ILO), uri: https://ilostat.ilo.org/data/bulk/, publisher: ILOSTAT, type: external database, date accessed: January 17, 2026
wdi-SL.IND.EMPL.ZS.definition: Employment is defined as persons of working age who were engaged in any activity to produce goods or provide services for pay or profit, whether at work during the reference period or not at work due to temporary absence from a job, or to working-time arrangement. The industry sector consists of mining and quarrying, manufacturing, construction, and public utilities (electricity, gas, and water), in accordance with divisions 2-5 (ISIC 2) or categories C-F (ISIC 3) or categories B-F (ISIC 4).
wdi-SL.IND.EMPL.ZS.prompt: What share of employed people in {place} worked in industry in {year}?
wdi-SL.IND.EMPL.ZS.scope: ILO modelled estimate. Includes manufacturing, mining, utilities and construction.
wdi-SL.IND.EMPL.ZS.route: Think of factories and building sites together. Compare their likely workforce with those of farms, retail, transport and public services.

wdi-BX.TRF.PWKR.DT.GD.ZS.label: Personal remittances, received (% of GDP)
wdi-BX.TRF.PWKR.DT.GD.ZS.definition: Personal remittances comprise personal transfers and compensation of employees. Personal transfers consist of all current transfers in cash or in kind made or received by resident households to or from nonresident households. Personal transfers thus include all current transfers between resident and nonresident individuals. Compensation of employees refers to the income of border, seasonal, and other short-term workers who are employed in an economy where they are not resident and of residents employed by nonresident entities. Data are the sum of two items defined in the sixth edition of the IMF's Balance of Payments Manual: personal transfers and compensation of employees.
wdi-BX.TRF.PWKR.DT.GD.ZS.prompt: How large were personal remittances received by {place} in {year}, relative to its economy?
wdi-BX.TRF.PWKR.DT.GD.ZS.scope: Use the World Bank’s personal remittances received as a share of GDP.
wdi-BX.TRF.PWKR.DT.GD.ZS.route: Estimate workers living abroad and money sent home per worker, then compare that flow with what the home economy produces in a year.

wdi-SP.POP.65UP.TO.ZS.label: Population ages 65 and above (% of total population)
wdi-SP.POP.65UP.TO.ZS.provider: World Population Prospects, United Nations (UN), publisher: UN Population Division
wdi-SP.POP.65UP.TO.ZS.definition: Population ages 65 and above as a percentage of the total population. Population is based on the de facto definition of population, which counts all residents regardless of legal status or citizenship.
wdi-SP.POP.65UP.TO.ZS.prompt: What share of residents in {place} were age 65 or older in {year}?
wdi-SP.POP.65UP.TO.ZS.route: Think about past family sizes and survival into old age. A long-lived population can still have a small older share when birth cohorts are growing quickly.

wdi-SH.DYN.MORT.label: Mortality rate, under-5 (per 1,000 live births)
wdi-SH.DYN.MORT.definition: Under-five mortality rate is the probability per 1,000 that a newborn baby will die before reaching age five, if subject to age-specific mortality rates of the specified year.
wdi-SH.DYN.MORT.prompt: At {year} mortality rates, how many children in {place} would die before age five per 1,000 live births?
wdi-SH.DYN.MORT.scope: Use the UN Inter-agency Group estimate published by the World Bank. This is a probability expressed per 1,000 births.
wdi-SH.DYN.MORT.route: Consider infant survival, clean water, nutrition and routine health care. Think about risks across five years instead of only at birth.

wdi-EN.POP.SLUM.UR.ZS.label: Population living in slums (% of urban population)
wdi-EN.POP.SLUM.UR.ZS.provider: Urban Indicators Database, UN Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat), uri: https://data.unhabitat.org/
wdi-EN.POP.SLUM.UR.ZS.definition: Population living in slums is the proportion of the urban population living in slum households. A slum household is defined as a group of individuals living under the same roof lacking one or more of the following conditions: access to improved water, access to improved sanitation, sufficient living area, housing durability, and security of tenure, as adopted in the Millennium Development Goal Target 7.D. The successor, the Sustainable Development Goal 11.1.1, considers inadequate housing (housing affordability) to complement the above definition of slums/informal settlements.
wdi-EN.POP.SLUM.UR.ZS.prompt: What share of the urban population of {place} lived in households classified as slums in {year}?
wdi-EN.POP.SLUM.UR.ZS.scope: Use the published UN-Habitat series. It considers deprivations in water, sanitation, living space, housing durability or tenure.
wdi-EN.POP.SLUM.UR.ZS.route: Estimate the scale of informal or severely underserved neighbourhoods in the largest cities, and account for conditions in smaller towns.

wdi-SE.PRM.ENRL.TC.ZS.label: Pupil-teacher ratio, primary
wdi-SE.PRM.ENRL.TC.ZS.provider: Stat Bulk Data Download Service, UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), uri: https://uis.unesco.org/bdds, publisher: UNESCO Institute for Statistics (UIS)
wdi-SE.PRM.ENRL.TC.ZS.definition: Primary school pupil-teacher ratio is the average number of pupils per teacher in primary school.
wdi-SE.PRM.ENRL.TC.ZS.prompt: How many primary pupils were there per primary teacher in {place} in {year}?
wdi-SE.PRM.ENRL.TC.ZS.scope: National pupil–teacher ratio. It can differ from the headcount in a classroom.
wdi-SE.PRM.ENRL.TC.ZS.route: Picture an ordinary class, then allow for specialist teachers, classes that share teachers and very small rural schools.

wdi-SH.MED.NUMW.P3.label: Nurses and midwives (per 1,000 people)
wdi-SH.MED.NUMW.P3.definition: Nurses and midwives include professional nurses, professional midwives, auxiliary nurses, auxiliary midwives, enrolled nurses, enrolled midwives and other associated personnel, such as dental nurses and primary care nurses.
wdi-SH.MED.NUMW.P3.prompt: How many nurses and midwives were recorded for every 1,000 residents in {place} in {year}?
wdi-SH.MED.NUMW.P3.scope: Use the reported nursing and midwifery personnel series.
wdi-SH.MED.NUMW.P3.route: Estimate nurses per hospital ward and shift, then include clinics and maternity care. Compare staffing with the population the facilities serve.

wdi-AG.LND.AGRI.ZS.label: Agricultural land (% of land area)
wdi-AG.LND.AGRI.ZS.provider: FAO electronic files and web site, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
wdi-AG.LND.AGRI.ZS.definition: Agricultural land refers to the share of land area that is arable, under permanent crops, and under permanent pastures. Arable land includes land defined by the FAO as land under temporary crops (double-cropped areas are counted once), temporary meadows for mowing or for pasture, land under market or kitchen gardens, and land temporarily fallow. Land abandoned as a result of shifting cultivation is excluded. Land under permanent crops is land cultivated with crops that occupy the land for long periods and need not be replanted after each harvest, such as cocoa, coffee, and rubber. This category includes land under flowering shrubs, fruit trees, nut trees, and vines, but excludes land under trees grown for wood or timber. Permanent pasture is land used for five or more years for forage, including natural and cultivated crops.
wdi-AG.LND.AGRI.ZS.prompt: What share of land in {place} was used for agriculture in {year}?
wdi-AG.LND.AGRI.ZS.scope: Include arable land, permanent crops and permanent pasture.
wdi-AG.LND.AGRI.ZS.route: Sketch the country’s terrain and estimate the share covered by crop fields or grazing land. Dry rangeland may count even where few crops grow.

wdi-SI.POV.GINI.label: Gini index
wdi-SI.POV.GINI.provider: World Bank, Poverty and Inequality Platform. Data are based on primary household survey data obtained from government statistical agencies and World Bank country departments. Data for high-income economies are mostly from the Luxembourg Income Study database. For more information and methodology, please see http://pip.worldbank.org., World Bank (WB), uri: http://pip.worldbank.org, note: Data are based on primary household survey data obtained from government statistical agencies and World Bank country departments. Data for high-income economies are mostly from the Luxembourg Income Study database.
wdi-SI.POV.GINI.definition: Gini index measures the extent to which the distribution of income (or, in some cases, consumption expenditure) among individuals or households within an economy deviates from a perfectly equal distribution. A Lorenz curve plots the cumulative percentages of total income received against the cumulative number of recipients, starting with the poorest individual or household. The Gini index measures the area between the Lorenz curve and a hypothetical line of absolute equality, expressed as a percentage of the maximum area under the line. Thus a Gini index of 0 represents perfect equality, while an index of 100 implies perfect inequality.
wdi-SI.POV.GINI.prompt: What was the published Gini index for {place} in {year}?
wdi-SI.POV.GINI.scope: The scale runs from 0 for complete equality to 100 for maximum concentration. The survey may measure income or consumption.
wdi-SI.POV.GINI.route: Imagine splitting income or consumption among five groups. Think how different their shares would be and compare with an evenly split distribution.

baseball-HR.label: HR
baseball-HR.prompt: How many home runs did the {team} hit in {year}?
baseball-HR.scope: Count home runs hit by the team during the regular season.
baseball-HR.route: Estimate home runs across an ordinary game and multiply by the number of games. Ballparks, lineups and era all affect that rate.

baseball-R.label: R
baseball-R.prompt: How many runs did the {team} score per game in {year}?
baseball-R.scope: Divide regular-season runs scored by games played.
baseball-R.route: Think about innings with runners on base and the fraction of those runners who score. One big inning can move the average.

baseball-attendance.label: attendance
baseball-attendance.prompt: How many fans did the {team} draw per home game in {year}?
baseball-attendance.scope: Reported season attendance divided by home games. Attendance can reflect tickets sold.
baseball-attendance.route: Estimate the ballpark’s capacity and how full it is on weeknights versus weekends. Include the less popular games when averaging.

baseball-SB.label: SB
baseball-SB.prompt: How many bases did the {team} steal in {year}?
baseball-SB.scope: Count successful steals in the regular season.
baseball-SB.route: Estimate opportunities with a runner on first and second base open, then the fraction with a successful steal. Tactics vary by era and lineup.

baseball-CG.label: CG
baseball-CG.prompt: How many complete games did pitchers for the {team} record in {year}?
baseball-CG.scope: Count regular-season games in which one pitcher pitched the entire game for the team.
baseball-CG.route: Think about how often the starting pitcher lasts through the last inning. Modern relief pitching has made complete games rare.

baseball-SO.label: SO
baseball-SO.prompt: How often did {team} batters strike out per 100 at-bats in {year}?
baseball-SO.scope: Batter strikeouts divided by official at-bats, times 100. Walks are excluded from at-bats.
baseball-SO.route: Estimate how often a batter makes an out and how often that out is a strikeout. Pitching and hitting styles vary by era.

baseball-BB.label: BB
baseball-BB.prompt: How many walks did the {team} draw per game in {year}?
baseball-BB.scope: Divide batting walks by regular-season games played.
baseball-BB.route: Estimate how many batters come to the plate in a typical game and the fraction who see four balls before the plate appearance ends.

baseball-RA.label: RA
baseball-RA.prompt: How many runs did the {team} allow per game in {year}?
baseball-RA.scope: Divide regular-season runs allowed by games played.
baseball-RA.route: Picture the average opposing batting lineup. Think of innings where pitching keeps the bases empty versus innings when several runners reach.

baseball-X3B.label: X3B
baseball-X3B.prompt: How many triples did the {team} hit in {year}?
baseball-X3B.scope: Count triples hit during the regular season.
baseball-X3B.route: Picture how often a ball reaches the deep outfield and a runner can make third before the throw. Ballpark shape matters.

baseball-SHO.label: SHO
baseball-SHO.prompt: How many shutouts did the {team} record in {year}?
baseball-SHO.scope: Use team pitching shutouts in the regular season.
baseball-SHO.route: Estimate how often the opposing team scores no runs. One bad inning is enough to prevent a shutout.
